html:
SMTO-FIL-0045 — SMTO couldn't set up this copy between Gateways

GUID: 9ebcba03-d4e6-4a18-88db-6696585a80ba
Slug: transfer-preflight
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • Before copying anything, SMTO checks both Gateways and the request. One of those checks failed, so the copy didn't start and no files were changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Gateway picker for your message (its menu is titled Execution target) and select both the Gateway that has the file and the one that should receive it. SMTO can only copy between Gateways that are selected for the request.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and check that both Gateways have their Enabled switch On and are connected; use Check connection on any that looks offline. SMTO won't start a copy if either Gateway is turned off, offline or shows Identity changed.
  3. Use Check for updates on both Gateways if either is out of date. Older Gateways may not support copying files between Gateways.
  4. Make sure the source and destination are different Gateways. To copy within one computer, ask SMTO to copy the file on that Gateway instead. A copy between Gateways needs two separate Gateways.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts the copy and reports that the file was copied and verified.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO's Gateways. Don't keep sending the same request unchanged; it will fail the same check until the Gateways or the request are corrected.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • gateway.copy did not start because no engine-authorized copy plan was present or copy_preflight.prepare rejected the request (argument schema, same source and destination Gateway, Gateway outside the run's selected targets, disabled, offline or identity-changed Gateway, missing file_transfer capability, or an unavailable working directory).

What this means

  • Gateway copy has no prepared transfer plan, or preflight cannot validate the intended endpoints, paths, scope or request fields. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway copy has no prepared transfer plan, or preflight cannot validate the intended endpoints, paths, scope or request fields.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the safe preflight reason and selected source/destination Gateway identities.

How to fix it

  • Read the preflight error text in the operation result. Confirm both Gateways are in the run's selected targets, enabled, connected or degraded, unchanged in identity and advertising the file_transfer capability, and that source_gateway differs from destination_gateway; correct the arguments or Gateway records, then resubmit. Nothing was opened on either Gateway.
  • Correct the reported source, destination, scope or limit using the supported transfer flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended supported transfer passes preflight before opening source/destination sessions.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
